chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:

It is not befitting for the divorced woman that she goes out except by the permission of her husband, until her waiting period is fulfilled by three quroo' (pure periods), or three months if she does not menstruate.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a divorced woman leaving her home during the waiting period in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the principle of *takhallu* (residence) during the *iddah*, emphasizing the husband's authority over the marital home to preserve lineage and facilitate potential reconciliation. It clarifies the duration of this waiting period as three menstrual cycles or three months for non-menstruating women, a ruling foundational to Shia jurisprudence regarding the rights and obligations of both spouses post-divorce. The requirement of the husband's permission for departure highlights the protective yet authoritative nature of the *iddah* period in maintaining family stability.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, and al Husayn Bin saeed, from Al Wasim Bin Urwat, from Abu Al Abbas, 
He<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘It is not befitting for the divorced woman that she goes out except by the permission from her husband, until she has fulfilled her waiting period by three Al-Quroo (pure periods), or three months if she does not menstruate’.
en.sarwar: 11. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad [from Muhammad ibn Khalid] and al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al- Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, that

it is not proper for a divorced woman to go out without the permission of her husband until waiting period is complete with three Hayd (menses)-free periods or three months if she does not experience Hayd (menses).”’
